t.2.88.1: Having dwelt for a long time on that mountain, he who loved the mountain and its forests, seeking to please Vaidehī and delighting his own heart as well,
t.2.88.2: Then the son of Daśaratha, resembling an immortal, showed the wondrous Citrakūṭa to his wife, as Puraṃdara shows it to Śacī.
t.2.88.3: Having seen this lovely mountain, O gentle lady, neither the loss of my kingdom nor separation from my friends troubles my mind.
t.2.88.4: Look, gentle lady, at this mountain, thronged with flocks of many kinds of birds and adorned with peaks rich in minerals that seem to pierce the sky.
t.2.88.5: Some are like silver, some resemble blood, some are yellow or madder-red in hue, and some shine with the radiance of the finest gems.
t.2.88.7: This mountain shines, surrounded by herds of various deer and by troops of leopards, hyenas and bears that are free from malice, and thronged with many birds.
t.2.88.6: Some regions of this lord of mountains, adorned with minerals, shine with the hue of flowers, of arka and of ketaka, and some glow with the radiance of the jyotīrasa gem.
t.2.88.8: With mango, rose-apple and asana trees, with lodhras, priyālas, jackfruit trees and dhavas, with aṅkolas, bhavyas and tiniśas, with bilvas, tindukas and bamboos.
t.2.88.10: Covered with these and other such trees, flowering, laden with fruit, shady and delightful to the mind, this mountain flourishes in splendor.
t.2.88.9: It is adorned with kāśmarī, ariṣṭa and varaṇa trees, with madhūkas and tilakas as well, with badarī and āmalaka trees, with nīpas, and with vetra, dhanvana and bījaka trees.
t.2.88.11: Look, gentle lady, at these high-spirited Kiṃnaras, kindling delight in love, sporting in pairs upon the lovely mountain plateaus.
t.2.88.12: See the charming swords hanging from the branches, and the fine garments too, left from the pleasure-ground of the Vidyādhara women.
t.2.88.13: With its waterfalls, its gushing springs, and its rills trickling here and there, this mountain shines like an elephant in rut, streaming with ichor.
t.2.88.15: If I dwell here for many autumns together with you, O blameless one, and with Lakṣmaṇa, grief will not consume me.
t.2.88.14: The breeze from the caves, carrying the fragrances of many kinds of flowers and coming near to delight the nostrils, what man would it not fill with joy?
t.2.88.16: O lovely lady, I have truly delighted in this charming place, rich in flowers and fruits, thronged with flocks of many kinds of birds, and crowned with wondrous peaks.
t.2.88.17: Through this dwelling in the forest I have gained a twofold fruit: my father's freedom from debt in the matter of dharma, and likewise what is dear to Bharata.
t.2.88.20: All around, the mountain's broad rocks gleam by the hundreds, abundant and many-hued, in blue, yellow, white and red.
t.2.88.18: Vaidehī, do you find delight here on Citrakūṭa with me, as you watch the many kinds of beings, disciplined in mind, speech and body?
t.2.88.19: The royal sages of old, my great-grandfathers, declared that this very dwelling in the forest is the nectar of kings, leading to their well-being after death.
t.2.88.21: At night the herbs of this lord of mountains shine in their thousands like a flame of fire, each a radiance of its own, blazing with splendor.
t.2.88.22: Some regions of this mountain look like dwellings, some resemble gardens, and some shine as though formed of a single rock, O lovely lady.
t.2.88.23: Citrakūṭa, risen high, shines as though it had split the earth apart; that auspicious peak of Citrakūṭa is seen from every side.
t.2.88.25: Look, O lady: garlands of lotuses, crushed and cast aside by lovers, are to be seen here, and fruits of many kinds as well.
t.2.88.24: Look at the lovely beds of the lovers, their coverlets made of kuṣṭha, puṃnāga, tagara and birch leaves, and strewn with lotus petals.
t.2.88.26: That mountain Citrakūṭa, rich in roots, fruits and water, seems to surpass even the lotus pond Vasvaukasārā and the land of the Northern Kurus.
t.2.88.27: But, my lady Sītā, having spent this time in delight with you and with Lakṣmaṇa, I shall attain a joy that increases the dharma of my family, standing firm on the path of the virtuous through my own supreme observances.
